newsitem.title: USA: Stocks weak in choppy trading.
newsitem.headline: Stocks weak in choppy trading.

text.p: Stocks fell Friday as investors continued to sell technology stocks and remained cautious after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's warning about excessive stock prices on Wednesday.
But some buyers emerged for the battered technology stocks and the broader market lifted off its lows.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was down 21.16 points at 6,903.91, after falling more than 50 points earlier.
"People got a little bit nervous," said Charles Pradillo, Cowen & Co. market analyst. "I think there's just fears that Greenspan might be out there waiting in the wings to tighten."
Greenspan on Wednesday questioned the sustainability of the market's sharp rise in testimony before Congress and hinted that the Federal Reserve may raise interest rates.
The stock market has been under a cloud since the Fed chairman's remarks. But traders and analysts said that a near-term fall in stocks was not a shock after the Dow drove through the 7,000 mark.
"In view of what's happened in the market, it shouldn't come as a surprise," said Alice Hook first vice president at McDonald & Co. "We had to see a pullback somewhere along the line."
Technology stocks bore the brunt of the early selling as investors followed through on Thursday's hammering of the group. "I think a lot of the momentum guys have gotten off these," Pradillo said.
On Thursday, the Nasdaq composite index sank 27.89 points, or 2.08 percent, to 1,312.66, the largest point drop since July 23.
Thursday's sell-off in technology stocks came after some analysts on Wall Street thought 3Com Corp.'s $6.6 billion takeover offer for U.S. Robotics Corp. was too low.
But after tumbling about 16 points, the Nasdaq composite was off just 1.98 points at 1,310.68 at 1 p.m. EST, as some buyers for leading tech stocks emerged.
Giving the Nasdaq composite support was heavyweight chip maker Intel Corp., which rose 3-1/64 to 142-3/4 after dropping to a session low of 137.
Elsewhere, Cigna Corp. said it signed a definitive agreement to acquire Healthsource Inc. for $21.75 a share. Cigna rose 2 to 154-5/8 and Healthsource gained 4-1/8 to 21.
General Cigar Holdings Inc.'s initial public offering jumped 5-5/8 to 23-5/8.
Intuit Inc. fell 1 to 24-3/8 after the financial software company said it expects slowing sales for at least the next two quarters.
